summary.headline: JSW Steel Q2 FY27: record crude output of 7.27 Mt and consolidated revenue of Rs.54,486 crore, with EBITDA margin at 18% and PAT of Rs.5,359 crore.
summary.overview: JSW Steel posted record consolidated crude steel production (7.27 Mt) and sales (7.46 Mt, up 13% YoY), with highest-ever domestic sales of 6.29 Mt. Adjusted consolidated EBITDA was Rs.9,941 crore (18% margin), held back by higher coking coal and iron ore costs and lower long-product realisations QoQ. Net debt fell to Rs.44,482 crore, with leverage at 1.28x and gearing at 0.39x. The Board approved about Rs.26 Mt of additional capacity projects, lifting the capex plan to Rs.1.48 lakh crore over 5 to 6 years from Rs.1.3 lakh crore.

financial_highlights.change: Realisations fell QoQ, mainly long steel prices
Gross debt down more than Rs.29,000 crore in H1
PAT loss due to Rs.276 crore stamp duty provision (BPSL transaction); PAT positive excluding it
Up 77% YoY; steel volumes up 53%; credit GMV about Rs.2,400 crore, up 91%

segments.name: India operations
segments.commentary: Crude steel 7.07 Mt (record, up about 5% YoY) at about 88% utilisation; sales 7.27 Mt (up 14%), with domestic sales 6.29 Mt (up 12%). BF-3 Vijayanagar reached about 90% utilisation after late-June light-up.

segments.name: Value-added and special products
segments.commentary: Record sales of 4.11 Mt, up 11%. Institutional sales up 15%, auto sales a record and up 36%, appliance up 28%, renewables up 14%.

segments.name: Overseas (Ohio, Texas, Italy)
segments.commentary: Sequentially better on higher realisations. US operations generated about $19 million EBITDA; Italian rail mill EUR 7 million, flat QoQ. Ohio and Texas had September maintenance/upgrade shutdowns.

segments.name: JSW JFE Steel (JJSL) JV
segments.commentary: Sales 0.92 Mt and EBITDA Rs.1,136 crore; approved 5 Mt expansion to 9.5 Mt capacity by FY31.

segments.name: JSW One digital platform (66% stake)
segments.commentary: GMV Rs.6,989 crore, up 77% YoY; platform reported positive EBITDA.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 volumes to rise on full production at Vijayanagar BF-3 and JVML.
Coking coal cost expected to rise by about $25/t in Q3, following the sharp increase in the latter half of Q2 (Q2 rise was about $10/t, vs earlier guidance of $12-15).
Iron ore cost marginally higher in Q3; management expects a softer iron ore environment over the next few quarters.
Price increases in October plus recovery of earlier losses to be fully reflected in the October-December quarter; management expects to offset cost increases and add to margin over Q2.
Domestic steel demand expected to grow 7-8% in FY27; on track to meet FY27 production and sales guidance.
Capacity target of 78 Mt in India by FY32 including JVs; total capex plan Rs.1.48 lakh crore over 5-6 years, mostly funded by internal accruals.
capex_capacity: Board approved Phase-2 of 5 Mt at JSW Utkal (Odisha), taking capacity to 10 Mt; Phase-1 due Q3 FY30, Phase-2 due Q1 FY31. Management pointed to about Rs.48,000 crore total for 10 Mt across both phases.
Added 8 Mt pellet plant at JVML Vijayanagar, plus extra converter and caster for JVML Phase-2, taking Vijayanagar crude capacity to 25 Mt.
Dolvi Phase-3: adding caster and plate processing, lifting CSP capacity to 7 Mt. Vasind CRM complex of 1.8 Mtpa due Q2 FY30.

Mozambique MdR coking coal (acquired March 2026): Board approved capex for about 9 Mt of cleaned prime hard coking coal, production from CY28. Captive coking coal linkage, including Illawarra (2 Mt) and domestic 3.5 Mt from washeries, totals about 15 Mt.
Slurry pipeline in Odisha on track for March 2027. Three Karnataka iron ore mines due Q4 FY27 (about 4 Mt; Karnataka total about 15 Mtpa). Parbatpur and Dugda washeries targeted next year.
Renewable energy: over 1,000 MW commissioned; 1.5 GW being commissioned, taking total to 2.5 GW+. Khopoli 0.5 Mt scrap processing centre: baler commissioned in Q2, shredder due by end-Q3 FY27.
demand_pricing: Indian steel consumption grew 7% in Q2 and 7.5% in H1 FY27. Management noted the draft National Steel Policy 2047 targets 505 Mt consumption by 2047.

Long steel prices fell sharply in June-July on monsoon, Middle East disruption and labour availability, then recovered in August-September on public capex. Flat prices corrected less and have since recovered.
Auto sector negotiations for the next quarter are ongoing with no indication given; the previous quarter's auto negotiations are closed. The price differential was not disclosed.

Coking coal near $270/t per management's cited peer context; management said elevated prices apply industry-wide. Iron ore in India is flattish in rupee terms, with NMDC Chhattisgarh derailment and monsoon disruptions.
Long products: integrated producers hold about 30-35% of the market; secondary producers hold 65-70%, driving volatility.
China steel production down about 3% and consumption down about 4% in Jan-Sep; China finished steel exports down 2% while total exports including semis rose 3.3%.

qa_highlights.question: Capex sizing: would JVML Phase-2 (5 Mt) cost about Rs.10,000 crore more than Utkal Phase-2 (5 Mt)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to about Rs.48,000 crore for 10 Mt across Odisha Phase-1 and Phase-2 combined, and said the JVML Phase-2 scope includes a hot strip mill that Utkal Phase-2 lacks.

qa_highlights.question: Does the JV capex raise leverage to as high as 10x net debt/EBITDA, and is JSW Steel ring-fenced?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Swayam Saurabh said net debt/EBITDA will not reach 10x, may rise slightly during the project phase, and JSW Steel is ring-fenced by design. JV-level net debt as of September 2026 was referred to the IR team for one-to-one follow-up.

qa_highlights.question: Coking coal outlook and margin impact in H2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said elevated prices are industry-wide, with Q3 cost up about $25/t already in estimates. Domestic washeries and Mozambique supply are expected to offset part of imported cost.

qa_highlights.question: Risk to capex numbers from rupee depreciation, and execution risk across multiple simultaneous sites?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the INR cost estimates include normative currency depreciation and hedging costs over the capex period. Management said labour is better available in the east and in-house expertise is being redeployed, with two or three large contracts planned for blast furnace and melt shop work.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management in funding Rs.1.48 lakh crore capex through the cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the plan does not depend on high steel prices. Cash generation of about Rs.25,000-30,000 crore a year is expected to largely self-fund, and the company has room to borrow temporarily at 1.28x leverage. Q2 generated free cash despite about Rs.6,500 crore capex.

qa_highlights.question: Dollar debt exposure and hedging?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said dollar exposure fell from over $6 billion at the start of last year to about $3.5-3.6 billion, with hedging extended beyond the historical 12-month policy. Management said a $500 million bond was repaid in October, preponed from April.

risks_watch: Coking coal prices elevated (management cited about $270/t) and Q3 cost step-up of about $25/t; margin protection depends on October price increases holding.
Iron ore supply tightness in India (NMDC Chhattisgarh derailment, monsoon disruption) versus flat international prices; management expects a softer trend in coming quarters.
Balance sheet build-up: net debt/EBITDA may rise above 1.28x during peak capex; JJSL/BPSL standalone net debt not disclosed on the call.
Execution risk on multiple simultaneous greenfield and brownfield projects, plus contractor and labour availability.
Long-product price volatility driven by secondary producers, and the possible removal of safeguard duties on imports.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on demand and capex funding, with management stressing a strong balance sheet and cash generation. Cautious on input cost inflation and iron ore, and evasive on the auto price differential, JV-level net debt and coking coal cost specifics, which were deferred to follow-up.
key_quotes: Crude steel production and consolidated and India operations were the highest ever at 7.27 million and 7.07 million tonnes, respectively, both growing by about 5% YoY.
We achieved our highest ever domestic sales at 6.29 million tonnes, up by 12%, outpacing the Indian market growth.
We don't believe net debt to EBITDA will go to 10x.
So, this capex build do not, you know, rely on a very significantly positive, let's say, steel prices.
Coking coal costs are expected to rise by about $25 in Quarter 3, in line with the sharp increase in prices in the latter half of Q2.
